Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the run-chase! West Indies players are out there in the middle. Muhammad Waseem and Aryansh Sharma are the openers for United Arab Emirates.
... THE RUN CHASE …

Right then, West Indies have posted 306 on the board and they would be backing themselves to defend this total. For UAE, it is about taking this game deep and not crumbling under the scoreboard pressure. An interesting chase awaits us. Stay tuned.

UAE will be proud of their bowling effort. They were looking down and out after a blistering opening stand but Ali Naseer got the wicket of Charles and then young Adhitya Shetty got the better of in-form King. Aayan Khan then bowled a brilliant spell in the middle overs and got two big wickets of Brooks and Chase which put West Indies on the back foot. Zahoor Khan then showed his full range and bowled superbly at the death to make sure that things don’t go completely out of the hands of UAE going into the second half.

West Indies started off with a bang with both Charles and King looking in brilliant touch. Both of them scored fifties and at one point in time, Windies look all set to cross 350. The 129-run opening stand was broken on the last delivery of the 17th over and West Indies just kept losing wickets at regular intervals as it often has been the case for them in the middle overs of a 50-over game. West Indies bat deep though and they still manage to cross 300 courtesy of a handy cameo of 37 off 24 balls from Odean Smith.

West Indies have been bowled out but they still crossed the 300-run mark. They would have got much more though after the start they got but UAE bowlers did well to pull things back. It is a tough total for UAE though and they need to bat well if they want to level the series here.

Commentary.Commentary: Drinks break! This is a rollicking start by the West Indies openers. Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the action to start as the two umpires make their way out to the centre. The United Arab Emirates players stride out to the middle and they are joined by the two West Indies openers. Johnson Charles and Brandon King will open the innings for West Indies. Ali Naseer will start with the new ball for United Arab Emirates. Let's play...

West Indies (Playing XI) - Johnson Charles, Brandon King, Shamarh Brooks, Shai Hope (C/WK), Keacy Carty, Kavem Hodge, Roston Chase, Yannic Cariah, Odean Smith, Akeem Jordan (On ODI Debut) (In for Keemo Paul), Dominic Drakes.

United Arab Emirates (Playing XI) - Muhammad Waseem (C), Aryansh Sharma (WK), Vriitya Aravind, Lovepreet Bajwa (In for Rameez Shahzad), Asif Khan, Basil Hameed (In for Rohan Mustafa), Ali Naseer, Aayan Khan, Sanchit Sharma (In for Karthik Meiyappan), Adhitya Shetty (In for Junaid Siddique), Zahoor Khan.
TOSS - The two captains are out in the middle. Shai Hope calls it correctly and West Indies have opted to BAT first.

Windies, on the other hand, would be pretty pleased with their effort in the last game. Their bowlers showed great discipline while Brandon King produced a brilliant century. One thing is for sure, we are going to be entertained by the Caribbean flavour which was quite evident in the last game. Can UAE fightback to level the series? Let’s find out. Toss and team news in a bit.

UAE had some positives in the last game with the debutant Ali Naseer showing great maturity under pressure. Aayan Khan with the ball also did a good job but overall, UAE need to show much more intent and killer instincts to outclass West Indies here.

Hello and a very warm welcome to the second game of this three-match ODI series between the United Arab Emirates and West Indies. The battlefield is the iconic Sharjah Stadium again and it is an opportunity for the Windies to seal the series with another strong performance. The home team, UAE, on the other hand, need to pull up their socks and show better application in this game to take this series to the decider.
